sentences.text: Present: - Smt. Suvarna K. Mirji, B.Com., LL.B.[Spl]

Xiii Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge,
 Bengaluru.
Dated this the 14th day of March 2022

CRIMINAL APPEAL No.25022/2018  Appellant: 1) Sri. Subramani S/o Late Venkataperumal,
 Aged about 58 years, R/at No.2, 3rd Cross,
 Car Street, Halasuru, Bangalore-560 008.
(Rep by Sri. S.J. Sangavi Advocate)

V/s  Respondent: 1) State of Karnataka by  Halasuru Police Station, Bengaluru.
 Represented by Public Prosecutor,
City Civil Court Complex, Bengaluru.
(Rep by Public Prosecutor)
: JUDGMENT:

The appellant/accused has preferred this appeal U/sec 374(3) of Cr.PC praying to set aside the Judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the X ACMM, Mayohall Unit, Bengaluru in CC.No.23261/2010 on 07/02/2018 for an offence punishable Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 U/s 420 of IPC and Sec.7 & 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954.
2.
The appellant is accused and respondent is complainant before court below.

The rank of both parties are referred as referred before the court below.
3.

The brief facts of prosecution/respondent case is as under:-
The complainant/CW.1 received credible information about manufacturing of adulterated ghee and selling the same on 19/06/2010 at about 6-45 p.m. and that he and his staff proceeded and reached around 7-10 p.m at No.2, 3 rd Cross, Car Street,
Halasuru, Bengaluru and found one goods auto in front of the house and the driver was transporting the oil tins from the auto to the house and on enquiry he informed that on the advise of accused he is doing so and after entering into the house premises Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 he found accused who admitted that the said godawan belongs to him and that the CW.1 alleged to have enquired the appellant regarding vanaspathi and other articles in the godown and initially the appellant did not give proper answer and later on he admitted that he is ) Sri. Subramani S/O Late ... vs ) State Of Karnataka By on 14 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142786550/
1 manufacturing the adulterated ghee by mixing cooking oil, vanaspathi and fragrance and manufacturing duplicate ghee and knowingly fully well that it was adulterated ghee was selling the same in the open market under the brand Sri Krishna Ghee and New Radha Krishna Pure Ghee without any valid license and permit and thereby accused cheated the public and thereby committed an offences punishable U/s 420 of IPC and Sec.7 & 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954.
4.
The trial court taken cognizance against accused for an offence punishable U/s 420 of IPC and Sec.7 & 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954.
The trial court framed the charge against the accused and accused denied the same and claims to be Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 tried.

The prosecution examined witnesses PW.1 to PW.4 and marked ExP1 to ExP8(a) and MO.1 to MO.4 and thereafter trial court recorded statement of accused U/s 313 of Cr.PC, the accused denied the same and submitted no defence evidence.

Thereafter hearing arguments trial court pronounced the Judgment on 07/02/2018 convicting the accused for the offence punishable U/s 420 of IPC and sentenced the accused to undergo S.I for one year and pay fine of Rs.5,000/-, in default of payment of fine further undergo S.I for two months.

Further the accused is convicted for the offence punishable U/s 7 & 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to undergo S.I for a period of one year and shall pay fine of Rs.500/- and in default of payment of fine he shall further undergo S.I for 7 days and further ordered of sentences shall run concurrently.
Aggrieved by the said conviction Judgment the accused/appellant preferred the present appeal on the following grounds.
Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 5.
The appellant/accused submits that the magistrate has committed error in taking cognizance of the offence and as such the conviction is bad in law.
The magistrate erred in accepting and acting upon Evidence of Prosecution which is being inadmissible.
The evidence taken by the magistrate is manifestly erroneous and argument employed by magistrate for convicting the appellant utterly unsustainable in law.

The magistrate failed to observe fact that there is lot of omissions and contradictions and improvements with respect to evidence adduced by prosecution witnesses and the same have been overlooked by the magistrate.

The magistrate failed to appreciate the fact that PW.1 has adduced in his evidence that he has seized 18 tins label containing RG adulterated ghee 'A'
to 'Z' labeled daldas weighing 15 kgs, two bottles of adulterated ghee on the spot in the presence of panchas and his staff i.e., CW.2 to CW.9.

But whereas in his cross- examination he has categorically stated that he has not seized the vessels or equipment which was used by the appellant to prepare Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 adulterated ghee which itself clearly falsifies the evidence of PW.1 to the extent that if in reality the PW.1 had seized the above articles alleged to have used by the appellant for manufacturing of adulterated ghee, the PW.1 must and should have also seized each and every articles which were alleged to have used by the appellant for manufacturing of alleged adulterated ghee and this important aspect has lost sight of by magistrate while passing the impugned judgment.

The magistrate failed to appreciate the fact that PW.1 has categorically stated in his evidence that he himself along with CW.2 to CW.9 were present at the spot at the time of alleged incident, seizure and drawing mahazar, but in order to prove the case of the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt, the prosecution in all examined four witness including PW.1 and has failed to examine other witnesses.

The magistrate further failed to note the fact that PW.1 & PW.3 ) Sri. Subramani S/O Late ... vs ) State Of Karnataka By on 14 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142786550/
2 are police officers and PW.3 has turned hostile as is evident from his deposition and PW.4 is alleged to have worked as Scientific Officer in FSL and retired Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 and no other independent witness has been examined to support the case of prosecution and even evidence of witnesses corroborates and contradicts each other and cannot be believed and inspite of that fact magistrate erred in convicting the appellant and on this score alone judgment of conviction is liable to be set-aside.

The magistrate gravely erred in convicting the appellant without appreciating fact that PW.2 has categorically admitted in his evidence that he has signed seizure mahazar in the police station and that he do not know what was seized by police and only on request of police he has signed seizure mahazar and no material objects were seized in his presence and police even have not shown the appellant to him which itself clearly establishes fact that complainant for the reasons best known to him has filed false and frivolous complaint against appellant accusing him for alleged offences and appellant at no point of time has committed any offence as alleged by prosecution and without considering this aspect, the magistrate has manifestly Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 erred in convicting appellant which is not sustainable in the eye of law and deserves to be set-aside.

The magistrate gravely erred in ignoring fact that in the evidence of PW.3 he speaks about seizure,
but does not speaks about arrest of appellant and he categorically admits that he did not had any difficulty in making the driver of the auto rickshaw as witness to the seizure mahazar, but in the case on hand admittedly he has not cited the said driver as witness to the case and further in his cross examination PW.3 has categorically admitted that at the time of mahazar CW.1 has not seized any ghee bottles.

This is contradictory to the evidence of PW.1 and clearly disproves the case put forth by prosecution and without appreciating the above aspects magistrate has erred in convicting the appellant and the same is liable to be set-aside.

The magistrate erred in not appreciating the fact that PW.4 has not examined alleged adulterated ghee sent by the Investigating Officer in proper manner and has given false report alleging that ghee examined by him is adulterated.

At the time of cross- Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 examination it is specifically asked to the PW.1 by the counsel of appellant that he is not qualified person to examine the adulterated ghee for which he has denied,
but has failed to produce any document in that regard to substantiate the fact that he is qualified examiner of adulterated ghee and as such judgment of conviction suffers from illegality and deserves to be set-aside.
The magistrate failed to observe another aspect that interested witnesses have not been examined by the prosecution this is fatal to the prosecution case.
The magistrate failed to observe the fact in the above case evidence of PW.1 to 4 contradicts to each other and hence said fact has been overlooked by Magistrate.
When such being actuality and factuality question of prima facie does not constitute against above named appellant.

The magistrate grossly erred in law in not observing the fact that as per version of prosecution one driver of auto rickshaw was present at the time of alleged incident when appellant alleged to have involved in manufacturing of adulterated ghee, but the Investigating Officer Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 has not recorded statement of above said person and also not cited him as witness and the prosecution has failed to produce single documents to show that appellant is involved in the alleged crime except vague and bald allegations.
The magistrate grossly erred in law in not observing the fact that the C.W.2, 4, 6 to 10 who are interested witnesses have not been examined.
This fact clearly shows that there is no prima facie establish and as such the appellant ought to have been acquitted.
That there are several weaknesses in the evidence of prosecution witnesses which have been overlooked by magistrate and evidence ) Sri. Subramani S/
O Late ... vs ) State Of Karnataka

By on 14 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142786550/
3 was sufficient to create suspicion.
The appraisal of evidence on record by magistrate thus suffers from illegality manifest error.
The finding of trial court was unreasonable and perverse.
The sentence passed by magistrate is too harsh and severe.
The impugned judgment is illegal, incorrect and improper and has resulted in miscarriage of justice.

The appellant/accused prays to allow the appeal setting aside the judgment pronounced by X ACMM, Mayohall Unit, Judgment Crl. A.
No.25022/2018 Bengaluru in CC.No.23261/2010 on 07/02/2018 for an offence punishable U/s 420 of IPC and Sec.7 & 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and acquit him.
6.
The lower court records.
The appellant counsel argued.
Public Prosecutor argued.
Perused records.
7. The Points arise for my consideration are as under.

1. Whether the interference of this court in the judgment passed by the Magistrate court on 07/02/2018 in CC No.23261/2010 in convicting the appellant/accused for the offence punishable U/s 420 of IPC and Sec.7 & 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 is needed?
2. What order?

8. My findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1: In Affirmative Point No.2: See final order for following:
:REASONS:
Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 9.
Point No.1:-
As per prosecution case there are witnesses CW.1 to CW.11.
The CW.1 PSI of Halasur Police Station Bengaluru is complainant and investigating officer, CW.2 and CW.3 are independent pancha witnesses, CW.4 is ASI of Halasur Police Station Bengaluru.

Further CW.5 is head constable and CW.6 to CW.10 are police constables of Halasur Police Station Bengluru accompanied for raid with CW.1 as per prosecution case,
CW.11 is Assistant Director of FSL, Madival, Bengaluru.
That out of CW.1 to 11 prosecution examined witnesses PW.1 (CW.1), PW.2(CW.3), PW.3 (CW.5), PW.4 (CW.11) before trial court.
10. The CW.1/PW.1
Mohammed
S / o Abdul Azeez deposed evidence that he was working as Police Inspector of Halasoor Police Station from March 2009 to July 2011.
On 19/06/2009 he has received credible information about manufacturing of adulterated ghee and selling of ghee.

There were stickers in the name of New Radhakrishna Pure Ghee, New Radhakrishna,
Gopikrishna.

There were 18 tins label containing RG adulterated ghee A to Z labeled dalda weighing 15 kgs, two bottles of weighing adulterated ghee, creative aromatics chemicals (Artificial Fragrance) was also found in scene of offence.
He has seized the above said articles on the spot in the presence of panchas and his staff.
The Mahazar was conducted from 7.15 p.m to 9 p.m.
He has enquired accused was present at scene of offence for that he replied that he himself was adulterating the ghee, for that he was not possessing any license from concerned authority.
Thereafter they arrested accused and took accused and seized articles to police station.
The complaint, FIR and mahazar are marked as ExP1 to ExP3.

The seized two sample ghee bottles,
label sheet in the name of new Radhakrishna Pure Ghee, Articles and Creative Aromatics Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 chemicals are marked as MO.1 to MO.4.
He has recorded statements of C.W.4 to CW.9.
He has recorded the voluntary statement of the accused and produced him before court.
He had sent MO.1 to MO.4 for examination of FSL and received report from FSL that said ghee is adulterated one.
After the investigation he came to know that accused was adulterating the ghee.
As the investigation was completed he has submitted the charge sheet to court.
The ExP4 is FSL report and ExP5 is voluntary statement of accused.
11. The CW.3/PW.2 Jayaram S/o Swaminathan deposed evidence that he signed on seizure mahazar now shown to him and his signature marked as ExP3(b).
The seizure mahazar was conducted in the year 2009.
He has signed on seizure mahazar in the police station.
He don't know what was seized by the police.
On the request of police he signed on seizure mahazar.
No material objects are seized in his presence and also police have Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 not shown him any accused person at the time of seizure mahazar.
Along with him nobody else has signed the mahazar.
12. The CW.5/PW.3
Shivadanda
Dowdthi S/o late Ramachandrappa is head constable deposed evidence in support of PW.1.

PW.4 P. Mallesh S/o Late Pillaiahaz is Scientific Officer at FSL,
Bengaluru from 1999 to 2012 and deposed evidence that on 25/08/2009 he received two sealed articles along with two sets of case records from P.I pertaining to this case.
The articles sent to him were sealed with sealed as ULS in red wax seals in-taxed and same were tallied with specimen seal sent by the I.O.
They are marked by articles No.1 & 2 by the I.O.
On 23/08/2010 he opened above said articles two medium sized plastic containers with plastic cap each containing above 500 grams of thick light yellow color pasty like substance having smell of ghee.
Each of articles containing chemical tests.

1) Moisture test 1.0.13% not more than 0.5%, 2) Reichert Value Judgment Crl. A.
No.25022/2018 1.16, 2.15 not less than 24, 3) Total fat 1.54.8%, 2.61.4% not less than 99.5%, 4)
Foreign Fat not detected in article Nos.1 & 2, 5) Bandouin Test-Red color developed in Articles No.1 & 2 positive for vanaspathi, 6) Presence of starch- not detected in articles Nos.1 & I 2, 7) Added coloring matter-Yellow color in Article Nos.1 & 2.
From said parameters he is of the opinion that same found in above stated article No.1 & 2 analysis not confirmed to standard of Ghee and is adulterated with vanaspathi (Dalda).

That on 07/09/2010 after examination remaining sample were packed in the same plastic container sealed with their laboratory seal and sent to concerned police ) Sri. Subramani S/O Late ... vs ) State Of Karnataka By on 14 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142786550/
5 station along with report and control specimen seal of FSL and ExP6 is acknowledgement issued by FSL and ExP7 is remainder requisition and ExP8 is sample seal and ExP4 is FSL report.
13.

The PW.1 is PSI is complainant and investigating officer, further PW.3 head constable working in Halasoor Police Station Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 and he was accompanied PW.1 for raid on the accused and he deposed evidence in support of prosecution case.

That PW.2 Jayaram S/o Swamynathan is an independent witness and as per prosecution case panchanama is conducted in his presence by complainant/CW.1 and seized M.O.1 to 4 articles from custody of accused.

But the said witness PW.2 turned hostile and he deposed the evidence that he signed on the panchanama in the police station and he do not know what was seized by police and on the request of the police he signed on seizure panchanama and no material objects were seized in his presence.
The material panch witness PW.2 turned hostile.
Further as per prosecution case CW.2 is another one independent witness, but the police have failed to secure the said witness and said witness was not examined by the prosecution.
Further PW.4 is ASI, CW.7 to 9 are police constables, these witnesses have accompanied PW.1 for raid on accused, but these witnesses were not examined by the prosecution before trial court.
But the material point is seizure of Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018 articles M.O.1 to 4 from custody of accused has to be proved by prosecution.
But the prosecution not examined all the witnesses cited in the charge sheet.
14. The trial court in its Judgment relying on the evidence of PW.1 who is complainant as well as investigating officer and relying on evidence of official witnesses PW.3 & 4 convicted accused.
But other material witnesses CW.2, 4 to 10 are not examined.

Hence it is just and proper to remand the case to trial court with direction to direct the prosecution to examine all material witnesses and also give opportunity to accused to lead his defence evidence if any and dispose off the case in due procedure of law.
Therefore interference of this court in the judgment pronounced by trial court is needed.
Therefore I answer point No.1 in Affirmative.

15. Point No.2:
Judgment Crl. A. No.25022/2018

In view of above discussion I proceed to pass following :ORDER:
The appeal filed U/s 374 (3) CR.P.C by the appellant/accused is hereby allowed.

The Judgment passed in CC.No.23261/2010 on 07/02/2018 by the Xth Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayohall, Bangalore is hereby set aside and matter is remanded back to Xth Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayohall,
Bangalore with direction to direct the prosecution to examine all material witnesses and then give opportunity to lead defence evidence if any and then dispose off the case in due procedure of law.
